correctness.rationale: For n>=8, graph distance exactly two between distinct triples iff they intersect (a common disjoint third triple exists). If m defender triples cover u points, all C(n-u,3) unused-ground triples must be labelled one, proving weight >=2m+C(n-u,3). Comparing m<=r-2, m=r-1, m=r, m>=r+1 yields the sharp three-residue lower bound. Equality forces disjoint triple blocks except one allowable overlap at residue one. The positive ordinary-adjacency constraint holds in every classified case. Labelled matching and one-overlap double-counting factors checked separately. Independent graph-BFS and support-enumeration, factorial, and construction programs reproduce exact finite cases 8<=n<=20 as described; the infinite theorem is by proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The problem is a natural intermediate invariant blending intersection-based hop defense and disjointness-based totality on a classical infinite Kneser family. A sharp mod-3 minimum law, complete and nontrivial optimizer rigidity, and exact factorial counts distinguish three disjoint-packing regimes; residue one uniquely admits an intersecting pair, unlike common trivial matching constructions. Not implied by a simple substitution from existing adjacency-based Roman minimum. The same support method can serve as a baseline for higher-rank and all-weight enumerations without claiming those results.
